reply_text:
Joe has rerun the demo in claude-7. I'm checking those records and reading the excursion at the same time.The ports have never been stored on any record today: the HUD's "didn't happen" list has been empty all along. Finding out why.I'm still tracing why the ports never get stored; it's in the service's background executor setup.Settled-turn evidence stopped being written at 00:10 UTC today, and ports go with it. Checking which path marks turns analysed since then.The live fix is in and claude-7's demo checks out. Now adding the notes to the excursion.㊥ (`"a new dialogue in the claude-7 repl"`) claude-7's demo works now, but it first exposed a fourth defect, and that one affects everyone. No turn record has had its ports stored all day, and no settled turn has been written to the evidence store since 00:10 UTC. So the HUD's "didn't happen" list has always been empty. I've fixed it (futon3c `0ec902b6`, reloaded). With the fix, claude-7's turns read as intended. The order-of-work notes are in E-agency-work-orders, as you asked (`c49bb46c`).

㊩ (the fourth defect)
- **The cause.** The 象 seats publish their readings with `session_turn_analysis.py`. That script writes the reading file and the "analysed" flag directly, and never calls the JVM step that writes the evidence and computes the ports.
- **Why the tests didn't catch it.** The tests all published through the JVM, so they passed throughout.
- **The fix.** When the JVM's reaper sees a published reading, it now does the settling itself.
- **What has and hasn't been redone.** I recomputed ports for claude-7's three turns only. Today's other ~200 records still have no stored ports. I can backfill them, but it means about 200 writes to futon1b, so I haven't done it without asking.

㊢ (claude-7's session, now)
- **Turn 1.** The 🈯 question and the 🈸 offer are open. Your request for two questions is closed by claude-7's 🈯 paragraph, because its bracket quotes your words "should be called elephant.txt".
- **Turn 2.** Both questions close. There is one acceptance, of option 1, and an obligation on claude-7 to you.
- **Turn 3.** The 🈸 question about deleting the file is open, as intended.
- **"Do it in a new git repo…"** stays open even though it was done. claude-7's report bracket quoted only "yes 1", which is too short to link. claude-5 quoted the request itself, and that closed it.
- **The commit.** It isn't linked to the offer, because commits in a /tmp repo aren't captured. So claude-7's obligation still shows as owed.

㊢ (what went into E-agency-work-orders)
- **A third case: the claude-6 relay.** It traces the chain from you to claude-2, claude-4 and codex-23, and records that 象 can't see it today because no bell is recorded.
- **The revised order of work:**
  - bells and whistles recorded as turns (discovery first);
  - bells carry the proforma, which is your decision;
  - links across seats;
  - the demo extended to a relayed two-part request.
- **What the demos showed:** all four defects, with commit shas.

🈸 (one decision) Shall I backfill ports for today's records, and then start the discovery pass for bells as turns (step 1)?

previous_reply_acts.text: (`"we need the features we are building, and not just for me"`) Yes. The claude-6 case is exactly what the ledger is for, and today it can't see it. 象 only reads turns typed into a REPL: 727 since 3 October, plus 6 from Matrix. Bells between agents aren't recorded at all. So the path your request took (claude-2, then claude-4, then folded into codex-23's packet) has no acts and no open ports, and nothing can notice that half of it was never answered. To catch it, bells have to become turns in the ledger: a request opens a port, the completion bell answers it, and a relayed request stays linked to the one it came from.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(how the claude-6 case would look with that in place)
- **Your endorsement.** Your endorsement of the idea is an act in claude-6's session.
- **claude-2's bell to claude-4.** It relays the idea and opens a port in claude-4's ledger, linked back to your act. The link exists if the bell quotes your words in a bracket, which is the same mechanism I built today for replies.
- **claude-4 folds it into codex-23's packet.** That opens a second port, linked to the first.
- **codex-23's answer.** It covers the reload question only. The capture question stays open on claude-4's port, and therefore on yours.
- **The reminder machine.** It nudges whoever holds the oldest open link, here claude-4, instead of you finding out weeks later.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(order of work)
1. **Record every bell and whistle as a turn** of the caller–recipient pair, with the completion bell as its reply. The pair's turns get the same acts and ports as REPL turns. I'd first make a discovery pass: where in Agency to hook it, how many bells a day there are, and what reading them with 象 would cost. Then build it.
2. **Mark bells with the proforma.** At present CLAUDE.md says bells are not marked. Asking for one mark per request, with your quoted words in the bracket when relaying something you said, makes each request a separate act. So "two questions in one packet" becomes two ports instead of one. This changes CLAUDE.md, so it's your decision.
3. **Follow links across sessions.** The kernel today only makes agreements within one agent's session. A relayed request needs its port to stay open until the request it was relayed into closes.
4. **Rerun the demo**, extended so that claude-5 bells a second agent with half of a two-part request. The check: the unanswered half shows as open in both ledgers, and the reminder machine nudges the agent holding it.
